title: Improving the Lower Bound on Triangle Degree Sums Beyond (21/16)n

problemStatement.formal: \liminf_{n\to\infty} h(n)/n \geq c > 21/16, \text{ where } h(n) \text{ is the largest } k \text{ such that every graph on } n \text{ vertices with } e(G) > n^2/4 \text{ has a triangle } \{u,v,w\} \text{ with } d(u)+d(v)+d(w) \geq k. \text{ Conjecturally } c = 2(\sqrt{3}-1) \approx 1.4641.
problemStatement.plain: Turan's theorem forces a triangle once a graph on n vertices exceeds n^2/4 edges. The function h(n) measures the best guarantee on the sum of the three vertex degrees of some forced triangle. Fan (1988) proved h(n) >= (21/16)n = 1.3125n, and Erdos-Laskar proved h(n) <= 2(sqrt(3)-1)n ~ 1.4641n. The goal is to push the lower bound strictly above (21/16)n, narrowing this open gap.
